root_cause: ReprHighlighter's url regex character class [-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~]* did not include '@', so the URL match stopped at the first '@' (e.g. https://www.youtube.com/@LinusTechTips got highlighted only up to 'youtube.com/').
best_solution: In rich/highlighter.py, ReprHighlighter.highlights, append '@' to the url group's character class: r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~@]*)". The statement says outright 'Added @ in rich.highlighter:ReprHighlighter url regex pattern'. '@' is a valid URL character (userinfo, path segments like YouTube/Twitter handles), so widening the allowed set makes the whole link match one repr.url span. No other code changes.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_highlighter.py parametrized highlight_tests gains ("https://www.youtube.com/@LinusTechTips", [Span(0, 38, "repr.url")]), inserted right after the ' http://example.org/index.html#anchor ' case at line ~134. That means one url span covering the whole 38-char string, with no split spans. Any placement of '@' inside the character class passes.
locating_signals: The statement names the file, class and pattern: 'rich.highlighter:ReprHighlighter url regex pattern'. The title says '@ breaks highlighting in hyperlink'. grep for 'P<url>' finds the single line.
our_outcome_summary: Only v8 passed. v8 made the gold edit ('@' appended at the end of the class) plus a stray reproduce_issue.py, which did no harm. v4: empty patch; LiteLLM ContextWindowExceededError (28.7k prompt + 4096 output > 32768) after 10 tool calls, 321 s. v6: byte-identical source fix to gold, but it also added its own test case to tests/test_highlighter.py at the same spot (after the '#anchor' case, line 134) where the hidden test_patch inserts. git apply of the test_patch failed ('patch failed: tests/test_highlighter.py:134') and the task was scored unresolved, so a correct fix was lost to a test-file conflict. v7: put '@' in the right class but left a doubled trailing comma ('...~]*)",,'), which is a SyntaxError in rich/highlighter.py. Importing rich.console crashed pytest collection. It also edited the test file (at a different hunk). 110 calls, and it never re-imported the module after editing.
generalizable_lesson: (1) Do not edit existing test files. Hidden tests are applied as a patch on top of your diff, and an agent-added test at the same hunk makes the test_patch fail to apply, which turns a correct fix into a fail. If you want a regression test, put it in a new scratch file and delete it before finishing, or strip test-file changes from the final diff. (2) After any regex or literal edit, re-import the edited module (python -c 'import pkg.mod') or run the nearest existing test file. A one-character slip like ',,' is a SyntaxError that breaks every test. (3) When a PR-description statement names the file, symbol and exact change, make that minimal edit early. Do not spend context exploring until it overflows.
